title: Thanksgiving In Amsterdam, The Best of Times, The Worst of Times And (The Old) High Times Cannabis Cup

content_html_sanitized:
Work, work, work! Over a period from 1993 to 2004, as best I can recall, I think I went to most of the annual High Times Cannabis Cups in Amsterdam, always held on American Thanksgiving weekend. (I was the guy in the coat and tie, although some of my best friends were hippies.)

Originally, it was actually a part of my job as National Director of NORML, then for MarijuanaNews in Vancouver for Marc Emory’s Pot.TV, which was rudely interrupted by the US Drug Czar.

See

The Paupers of Pot and the Politics of Cannabis Prohibition In Canada. The Other Cases Raise Questions That Canada Must Answer. Will Canada Murder Michelle Rainey?

 

For most of the Americans, it was a real experience with “culture shock”. What is this thing called freedom? What is this place that they didn’t have to hide? Where they didn’t have to fear the people who were supposed to protect them…

This was illustrated by a joke that developed among the Americans because of the spelling of the Dutch word for “Police”, Politie, which looks like (but is not pronounced like) Polite, which was not what they associated with American police.

As regular readers of MarijuanaNews may gather, I am a great believer in competitive capitalism, and for all its countercultural appearances, there was intense competition for the various “Cups” for the various strains, developed by the coffeeshops.

I was never a judge, but I am happy to call most of the winners old friends. And they are still there, and Amsterdam, and The Netherlands are still free. 

Remember Coffeeshops are not just in Amsterdam, but in almost every Dutch town.

See

Haarlem On My Mind -- Plus A Belated Report on the 2000 Cannabis Cup.

Happily Dutch freedom is no longer unique, at least for the moment.

See

Cannabis Is In, Booze Is Out at This Year’s Thanksgiving Table

“The idea of going “California sober” is no longer taboo for many families on Turkey Day — THC is even showing up in the turkey itself.”

I am happy to report that I am going to Amsterdam next month to celebrate the fiftieth anniversary of The Bulldog, and the CoffeeShop system, but in the meantime, eternal vigilance is still the price of liberty.

Also, for the long holiday weekend, let me recommend three great movies (all musicals) that are each relevant in different ways.

The first would have to be Woodstock, the ultimate countercultural event, where almost half a million young Americans got together, peacefully in 1969, which terrified the entire country. How unAmerican! Remember, the Sixties were not about a Placebo.

See

As Budweiser-Sponsored Woodstock Burned, Beer Lobby Kills Proposal To Include Alcohol In Czar’s Prohibitionist Propaganda Campaign

The second would be Hair, which wasn’t produced until 1979, but was based on the Broadway musical from 1968, a year before Woodstock. Hippies really were a real thing, but totally unrealistic.

And then, Cabaret, from 1972, but based in 1931 Berlin, at the end of the socially liberal Weimar Republic, just before the Nazis came to power.

(The Nazis never got a majority of the votes before seizing power. The German establishment thought that they could control Hitler, and “work with him.” The Hippies weren’t the only ones who have been totally unrealistic.)

See What The Hemp Ban Reveals About The Condition of Our Democracy
